one_month_reasoning: No Hudbay-specific scheduled event is confirmed inside 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31: Q2 results came out on 29 July and Q3 results have historically come in early-to-mid November (no Q3 2026 call date announced as of today), so they probably fall just outside the window. The things that can move the stock this month are the copper price and peer read-throughs: Freeport and Antofagasta Q3 reports in the second half of October, LME Week in mid-October (where the 2027 TC/RC talks get going; spot TCs are a record -$175.7/t, which shifts margin to concentrate sellers like Hudbay), and news on the US Section 232 refined-copper tariff (15% proposed from 1 Jan 2027). Reports that the decision was postponed caused a roughly 5% one-day drop in copper on 19 Sep. The tariff risk cuts both ways, since unwinding the US stockpile would add to the 962kt of visible exchange stocks. HBM is about 19% below its 52-week high after copper pulled back from its record. I have no strong momentum or reversal view, so I used a symmetric lognormal centred on $26.18 with monthly sigma of 0.63/3.5 = 18%.

fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E EV/EBITDA (EBITDA $1.35B x 7.5x, net cash $0.08B, ~442M shares -> $23.0) and an asset-by-asset SOTP/NAV at a deck near current spot (~$12.4B -> $28.0), weighted 30/70 to $26.5. Sell-side targets ($29.5-$43, mean ~$31-35) are a cross-check, not an input.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E adj. EBITDA $1.35B x 7.5x = EV $10.1B; + net cash $0.08B; / 442M shares = $23.0

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 run-rate is $1.28B, set at YTD-average copper of about $6.0/lb. Spot copper is about $6.4-6.6/lb, which adds roughly $0.5/lb x ~250Mlb = +$125M. Gold has fallen back to about $4.3-4.4k/oz. I took roughly half the spot uplift because Constancia grades will decline and 2027 production is flat to lower: $1.35B.

Capstone trades at about 6.4x LTM and about 5.5x CY26 EV/EBITDA. I gave HBM about a 1.5x premium for its Arizona growth pipeline (Copper World plus Cactus, now the third-largest copper district in North America), a net-cash balance sheet and its gold by-product hedge.

About 400M weighted-average shares in Q2 plus about 45M issued to Arizona Sonoran holders (0.242 per share on about 187M ASCU shares not already owned; consistent with ASCU holders owning about 11% of the combined company), net of timing.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Constancia/Peru $3.3B + Snow Lake/Manitoba $2.8B + Copper Mountain/BC $1.6B + Copper World 70% $2.6B + Cactus $1.3B + Mason/exploration $0.6B + net cash $0.1B + Mitsubishi deferred $0.18B - corporate G&A/closure $0.6B -> ~$12.4B / 442M = $28

inputs_detail.derivation: The 2023 PFS gave Phase 1 an after-tax NPV8 of $1.1B at $3.75/lb copper. I uplifted it for a $5.0-5.5/lb long-term deck (roughly +$1.1B per $0.5/lb), less the higher capex the DFS will show, then took 70% because Mitsubishi owns 30%.
Purchase price was about C$1.48B (about US$1.07B) in March 2026. I marked it up modestly for higher copper since then.

Each asset's 2026 guided output (Peru 75-90kt Cu; Manitoba 180-220koz Au; BC 25-35kt Cu) at roughly $5.25/lb copper and $3,800/oz gold long term, with consolidated cash costs below zero ($(0.45)-$(0.25)/lb), capitalised at about 6x unlevered FCF for the remaining mine lives.

bear.story: Copper corrects to about $4.5-5.0/lb. The 962kt of visible exchange stocks (double last year's) and an unwind of the US tariff stockpile overwhelm the mine-supply deficit. Gold drifts lower too, Copper World's capex in the DFS disappoints, and Peru community unrest under the new Fujimori government hits Constancia. EV/EBITDA lands around 6x on roughly $1.0B of EBITDA.

base.story: Copper stays around $5.75-6.5/lb on supply problems (Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula, Chile -6.6%) and near-zero or negative TCs. Copper World is sanctioned around year-end 2026 with Mitsubishi funding 30%. Operations hit guidance and the multiple holds at about 7.5-8x. The stock moves up toward NAV.

bull.story: Copper rises to $7+/lb as the deficit deepens (UBS sees $15,000/t by March 2027; Citi $15-17k), gold recovers above $4.5k, and the Copper World sanction re-rates HBM as a US copper developer. The stock trades up to the high end of analyst targets ($35-43).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $17 (roughly 35% down, still above the $14.34 52-week low), the market would be pricing copper durably under about $4.75/lb or an asset problem: a Constancia disruption from Peru unrest, a Copper World capex blowout or deferral, or an equity raise to fund Arizona. With a net-cash balance sheet and a negative cash cost, an ordinary pullback in metal prices should not take the stock there.

Q4 2026 results and 2027 production and cost guidance (Constancia grade profile)
Mitsubishi $180M deferred contribution due (within 18 months of the Jan 2026 close)

key_uncertainties: Copper price path: visible stocks have doubled to 962kt while mine supply is falling, and banks disagree on the 2026 balance (from a 590kt deficit at MS to a 300kt surplus at GS)
Section 232 refined-copper tariff timing and the US inventory unwind
Copper World DFS capex versus the 2023 PFS figure of $1.3B, and how much Hudbay funds at sanction
Gold price (Manitoba is a gold mine in practice; gold is about 20% below its January peak)
Peru social and political risk under the new Fujimori government in regions that voted against her
Exact post-ASCU share count (estimated at about 442M; not directly confirmed)
reasoning: HBM is Hudbay Minerals, a copper and gold producer in Peru, Manitoba and BC with an Arizona growth pipeline (Copper World 70% after the $600M Mitsubishi JV, and Cactus via the Arizona Sonoran acquisition closed June 2026). Q2 2026: adj. EBITDA $321M, TTM a record $1.3B, net cash of $80M, 2026 guidance reaffirmed and consolidated cash costs cut to $(0.45)-$(0.25)/lb. Industry evidence is mostly supportive. LME copper reached records around $14.8-15.1k/t in early September; mine output fell 1.1% in H1 (Chile -6.6%, Grasberg and Kamoa disruptions); spot TCs are a record -$175.7/t, so smelters are paying miners for concentrate; peers such as Antofagasta posted +72% H1 profit. The counterweights are visible inventories nearly doubled year on year, copper's tariff-driven trades (a 5% one-day drop on 19 Sep on reports of a postponement), gold about 20% below its January high, and Peru political risk. At about 442M shares the market cap is about $11.6B and EV about $11.5B, roughly 8.5x my 2027E EBITDA at near-spot prices, against Capstone at about 5.5-6.4x. So on a multiple basis HBM is fully valued ($23). On asset NAV at a $5.25/lb long-term deck with the Arizona optionality, I get about $28, below the $31-35 sell-side mean. My blended fair value is $26.5, about the current price. Scenarios: bear $17.5 / base $27.5 / bull $39 at 25/50/25 gives an expected value of about $28. I built the ladder as a lognormal mixture around those three cases (within-case sigma about 0.3); total dispersion is a bit below the 63% realized vol, on the view that copper volatility partly mean-reverts. The median is about $27.5, slightly above spot, reflecting the copper supply deficit and the deal pipeline. Research was limited: Twelve Data fundamentals and estimates were unavailable on the current plan, and the post-acquisition share count is my estimate rather than a reported figure.
